catalog_quote: The initial of every Mangde syllable is obligatorily marked for high or low tone. Therefore, we computed pitch measurements based on initial tone of the word and the means of pitch peak and average. The mean pitch for initial syllables with high tone was 197 Hz while the mean pitch for initial syllables with low tone was 165 Hz. By the second syllable, these tonal differences have nearly neutralized. High toned words had a mean pitch of 188 for second syllable and low-toned words had a mean pitch of 179 Hz for second syllable. It should be noted that in Mangde tone moves to the first syllable of a word if negative marker <ma-> precedes verbs or adjectives. Native speakers of Mangde also have the intuition that the first syllable of the word is somehow more prominent. Synchronically, tone in Mangde is contrastive on the first syllable following the sonorants and the palatal fricative. To…

new_statements.quote: The initial of every Mangde syllable is obligatorily marked for high or low tone. [...] By the second syllable, these tonal differences have nearly neutralized. [...] It should be noted that in Mangde tone moves to the first syllable of a word if negative marker <ma-> precedes verbs or adjectives. Native speakers of Mangde also have the intuition that the first syllable of the word is somehow more prominent. Synchronically, tone in Mangde is contrastive on the first syllable following the sonorants and the palatal fricative. Tone in these instances is realized by either high or low pitch.
new_statements.citation: Nishida, Fuminobu. 2012. Mangde (མང་སྡེ་པའི་ཁ།) in Bhutan [ブータン王国のマンデビ語]. 秋田大学教養基礎教育研究年報 14: 77-87.
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (11 pp scan with Acrobat text layer;.txt alongside). Sec. 3 'The Phonological System', 3.3 'Pitch' spans the foot of p. 81 and top of p. 82 exactly as located. Every sentence of the reported quote is present verbatim in the text layer (txt lines 241-263); the '[...]' gaps omit only the F0 sentences ('Therefore, we computed pitch measurements... 197 Hz... 165 Hz' and 'High toned words had a mean pitch of 188 for second syllable and low-toned words had a mean pitch of 179 Hz for second syllable'). Surrounding context read (pp. 80-83): syllable canon, consonant/vowel inventories with H/L superscript tone marks on every example word, then 3.3: obligatory H/L on the syllable initia…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mangde has a two-way (high/low) register tone whose contrast is carried by the word-initial syllable (largely predictable from onset voicing, contrastive after sonorants and the palatal fricative) and is nearly neutralised on later syllables; the tonal/prominent position is the first syllable of the (prefixed) word, which speakers perceive as the most prominent. No independent stress system is described. Nishida 2009 (Japanese, p. 69) adds the word melodies: H first syllable -> following syllables L; L first syllable -> second H, third L.
new_statements.exceptions: Negative prefix ma- attracts the tone to itself (tone moves to the new first syllable). Tone predictable (high after voiceless, low after voiced obstruents) except after sonorants and the voiceless palatal fricative.
new_statements.domain_note: Word domain (including prefixed verb/adjective forms); based on elicited citation forms with F0 measurements of first vs second syllables (197/165 Hz vs 188/179 Hz). Variety: Tshangkha (Tsangkha) village, Trongsa district.
new_statements.identity_note: Nishida's data (2009, 2012) are from the Tshangkha/Tsangkha (ツァンカ) village variety, Trongsa district, i.e. Mangdebikha proper east of the Black Mountains = Glottolog nyen1254 'Upper Mangdep' (language level; Glottolog lists dialects Chutobikha chut1248 and Phobjikha phob1239, neither of which is the variety described). Names used: Mangde, Mangdebikha, 'Nyenkha, Ngenkha, Henkha, Mangdekha. Glottolog's ref 'Glennon & Glennon 2003 Nehan organized phonology data' is a PNG language mis-filed under this glottocode.

sources.quote: The initial of every Mangde syllable is obligatorily marked for high or low tone. [...] By the second syllable, these tonal differences have nearly neutralized. [...] It should be noted that in Mangde tone moves to the first syllable of a word if negative marker <ma-> precedes verbs or adjectives. Native speakers of Mangde also have the intuition that the first syllable of the word is somehow more prominent. Synchronically, tone in Mangde is contrastive on the first syllable following the sonorants and the palatal fricative. Tone in these instances is realized by either high or low pitch.
sources.note: Sec. 3 'The Phonological System', 3.3 'Pitch' (pp. 81-82): every syllable-initial is marked high/low tone but the contrast is realised on the word's first syllable and nearly neutralised by the second (F0 means given); tone moves to the first syllable when negative ma- is prefixed; 'Native speakers... have the intuition that the first syllable of the word is somehow more prominent.' No use of the word 'stress'.
